question: Ravi bought a watch for ₹4,800, spent ₹200 on its repair, and sold it for ₹6,000. What is his profit percentage?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total CP = Base Price + Repair Cost = 4800 + 200 = ₹5,000

Profit = SP − CP = 6000 − 5000 = ₹1,000

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 = (1000 ÷ 5000) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost of the watch = ₹4,800

Repair cost = ₹200

Selling Price (SP) = ₹6,000

 
 CP: ₹5000
 (4800 + 200)

 
 SP: ₹6000

 
• 
 

 Profit: ₹1000
 Profit % = 20%

**Formula Used:**

Total Cost Price (CP) = Initial CP + Overhead Expenses

Profit = SP − CP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total CP = 4800 + 200 = ₹5,000

⇒ Profit = 6000 − 5000 = ₹1,000

⇒ Profit % = (1000 ÷ 5000) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 1/5 × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Percentage

If Selling Price is less than Cost Price, Loss occurs. Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). SP = MP − Discount.

Successive Profit/Loss

If two similar items are sold at the same SP, one at x% profit and the other at x% loss, there is always an overall net loss equal to (x² ÷ 100)%.
